newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan journalist sentenced for legal expose.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan journalist sentenced for legal expose.

text.p: The author of a best-selling book attacking corruption in Venezuela's judicial system has been sentenced to a year in prison and his book has been yanked from circulation, judicial officials said on Friday.

William Ojeda, whose "How Much a Judge is Worth" sold out last year, was found guilty this week of defaming two judges mentioned in the work detailing the byzantine proceedings that bedevil the Venezuelan legal system.
"My book is a mirror of the perverse state of Venezuelan justice," he told Reuters on Friday. "My crime? I denounced corruption, I gave names and so they found me guilty."
Ojeda, 26, a journalist with local Radio Caracas Radio, said the sentence gave him the choice between a year in jail or paying to have his court sentence published in the national press.
"People have offered to pay for the newspaper notices, but I said no. I'm proud to have written the book. I'm not going to be forced to my knees ... it's a matter of honour."
He said he expected to be taken to prison in late January.

In a country where prisons overflow with inmates waiting up to four years for trial, Ojeda noted his case was processed in 14 months, "whereas something of this sort would normally take between five and ten years."

Judicial reform, backed by a ground-breaking World Bank project, has recently moved into the centre of Venezuelan public debate with President Rafael Caldera proposing creation of a High Commission of Justice that would be responsible for reorganizing the courts and firing corrupt judges.
